correctness.rationale: The endpoint bridge is a direct valid operator identity for a finite sum of left regular inverse-semigroup partial-permutation matrices: M_{xi*}=conjugate(M_xi)^T; each row and column is finite, so the sup absolute row-sum ℓ∞ norm equals the sup absolute column-sum ℓ1 norm of M_{xi*}. Using the published p=1 reduced groupoid/semigroup canonical norm identity and the groupoid endpoint involution duality yields the canonical p=∞ reduced identity on C S. Supremum over arbitrary nonempty P gives simultaneous-exponent norm equality, with I-norm density and norm domination furnishing surjective completion. Morita equivalence for countable equivalent Hausdorff ample groupoids in all p then transports through these isometries. Importantly no claim about density of finitely supported vectors in ℓ∞ is used. Assumptions: no zero, Hausdorff universal groupoid/weak semilattice; the application assumes the published groupoid-equivalence theorem and compatibility.

value.rationale: The p=∞ endpoint of a new inverse-semigroup/groupoid Lp comparison is a natural structural gap: finite-support density arguments cannot work on ℓ∞. The row-sum/column-sum involution duality supplies a distinct analytic mechanism and unlocks simultaneous-exponent reduced completions and their Morita/K-theory transport across every nonempty exponent set. This is a motivated completion of a natural theorem, rather than a cosmetic endpoint relabelling.
